questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Describe how a boom sector reallocates labour
questions.stem: A software team's ticket asks why a mining boom can shrink a country's factory output even without new tariffs; explain the mechanism in one paragraph.

answer.exemplar: A mining boom raises demand for labour and non-tradable goods, pushing up wages and the real exchange rate; factories lose cost competitiveness and contract, a pattern known as Dutch disease, even with no new tariffs.

questions.explanation: The boom raises relative prices and wages, drawing resources out of tradables. Blaming tariffs misses the price mechanism entirely.
